current.text: He has a broken foot and will not be ready for the start of the season.
Josh expects him back around Thanksgiving, followed by a slow ramp-up.
Daniel Gafford is the likely opening night center. Josh has Gafford and Morez Johnson Jr. ahead of Lively on the depth chart.
Josh finds him almost impossible to draft in 10, 12 or 14 team leagues and says to ignore his ADP of 107.
He becomes a draftable fantasy player if he wins the starting job.
He is in the last year of his contract and becomes a restricted free agent next offseason.
Dusty May is the new head coach. It is unknown how he will split center minutes among Lively, Gafford, Powell and Johnson.
Dallas has a crowded frontcourt with many bigs and forwards who expect minutes.
Experts expect Dallas to make another move, possibly trading Gafford.
Dallas has a 4-4-4 schedule in the fantasy playoff weeks, probably the best in the league, but also a league-high 16 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He has a long history of lower body injuries, and his games played have dropped every season since his rookie year.
When healthy, he blocks shots at a high level and rebounds well.
He is a strong defender and a good roller, especially in the short roll.
His fantasy value comes from FG% and blocks, both league outliers. He makes no threes.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both value him at 0 USD (ranks 212 and 144), and he cost 3 USD in our league last season. With a broken foot, a return expected around Thanksgiving, a slow ramp-up and Gafford and Johnson ahead of him, skip him in the auction. Watch his return and whether he wins the starting job. If he starts, his FG% (72 percent projected) and blocks (1.6) make him a FAB target for punt 3PM builds, and Dallas's 4-4-4 playoff schedule helps, though its 16 back-to-backs are a risk for a big with his injury history.
